text:
amanda (prod-sre): paging oncall — seeing a big spike hitting /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings.bulk from multiple IP ranges. WAF 403s and 429s up, some 5xxs. Looks like credential stuffing + scraper farm. tagging @devon and @miguel. urgent mitigation needed :rotating_light:

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1921036784 - High error rate & WAF/ratelimit triggered - SEV:P1 - paging oncall group prod-sre - follow live-mitigation runbook.

devon (oncall): i'm on it. dashboards up now. what's the immediate customer impact? any dedicated customers affected?

amanda (prod-sre): hosted API keys mostly. top symptoms: 429s for many tenant keys, some 403s from WAF when UA+payload matches. No dedicated/private customers impacted AFAICT. spike is ~20x baseline rps from those CIDR blocks. sample metric snapshot:

```
metric: requests_per_sec
baseline: 120rps
peak (affected): 2400rps from 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/24
waf_hits: 1.2k/min -> 50k over 10m
error_5xx: increased from 0.2% -> 3%
```

miguel (edge-infra): i can push geo/CIDR rate-shaping + stricter per-key limits. recommend: apply temporary WAF block for UA regex + block repeat offenders >500 req/min, and disable batch endpoints for anonymous/hosted keys for 15m to cut surface area.

devon (oncall): do that. start with WAF UA rule and per-ip rate limit. do NOT touch dedicated/private accounts. we should whitelist known enterprise keys.

deploy-bot: Applied WAF rule 98761 -> block UA regex "(ScrapeBot|python-requests|curl)" for 10m; Applied rate-limit rule to 203.0.113.0/24 and 198.51.100.0/24: 60 req/min default, burst 120.

ashley (prod-ops): i'm drafting a comms template for the affected customers; sending DMs to the top-10 tenants now. can someone confirm list of enterprise keys to whitelist?

amanda (prod-sre): whitelist list: enterprise keys A1A, B2B — i'm DMing the IDs. Also sample access log showing credential-stuffing pattern:

```
POST /v1/generate 200ms 5.6kb
host: api.redwood.ai
user-agent: python-requests/2.28.1
authorization: Bearer sk_live_***
body: {"email":"victim@example.com","password":"guess123"}
repeat count: same email tried 300x from different IPs via proxy chain
```

miguel (edge-infra): also flipping default anonymous quota down from 1000r/m -> 100r/m for now. command: ```curl -X POST https://internal-config/api/quota -d '{"scope":"anonymous","rate":100}'``` - will apply in 30s.

devon (oncall): acknowledged. i'll take primary and handle playbook & postmortem. miguel, you'll continue infra mitigation after i handoff in 30m?

miguel (edge-infra): acknowledged. i'll maintain WAF rules and monitor for IP churn. if proxies rotate, we'll escalate to challenge (captcha) with cloudflare-like handshake.

ashley (prod-ops): customer comms draft: "We're currently mitigating elevated malicious traffic causing intermittent 429s for some hosted API keys. We've applied blocking rules and rate limits; dedicated/private customers unaffected. We're monitoring and will update in 30 minutes." posting to #incidents-updates after devon confirms.

amanda (prod-sre): collection checklist for postmortem: fingerprinting used, peak rps, list of affected customers + duration, mitigation actions + timestamps, false positives + rollbacks. please record all commands.

incident-bot: Incident 1921036784 marked IN_PROGRESS. Reminder set for 15m.

devon (oncall): quick status update: WAF blocks + CIDR rate-limits took effect ~2m ago. 429 rate for affected tenants down ~75% vs peak, overall error 5xx trending back toward baseline. holding mitigations for 1 hour, then reassess.

ashley (prod-ops): :thumbsup: publishing comms in 5 once devon confirms stable for 10m.

miguel (edge-infra): plan for rollback: after 60m, replace hard block with challenge (captcha) for those CIDRs and open up burst to 200r/m. will monitor new IP ranges and add them to match rules as needed.

devon (oncall): i will hand primary to miguel at 1921038884 (30m from now). miguel, continue monitoring and keep me posted in this thread.

amanda (prod-sre): initial RCA guess: credential-stuffing via proxy farm + automated scraping. mitigation worked but need better early detection (UA+rate+payload anomaly).

miguel (edge-infra): continuing mitigation. will escalate to legal if we see persistent targeted credential stuffing.

ashley (prod-ops): comms posted to affected customers and #incidents-updates. template saved in /docs/incidents/templates/credential-stuffing.md

devon (oncall): update 10m later: metrics holding stable. WAF counts steady, customer reports minimal residual 429s. reducing alert noise thresholds and marking incident as "mitigated" but leaving open for postmortem.

amanda (prod-sre): noting items for postmortem owners: monitoring gaps, CIDR block list, timeline of WAF rule ids, customer impact window. assigning doc owner to devon.

incident-bot: Incident 1921036784 moved to MITIGATED. Please file postmortem within 72 hours.

devon (oncall): handoff complete, ending oncall for this thread at 1921037100. thanks team :raised_hands:
